exposure: Delivery of the baby (during cesarean section)
cohort: Twenty-six women undergoing elective cesarean section in spinal anesthesia.
finding: Spinal anesthesia, delivery of the baby, and intravenous oxytocin each caused significant and distinct acute changes in maternal cardiovascular parameters, including blood pressure, heart rate, vascular tone, and cardiac ejection function.
mod_finding: Delivery of the baby resulted in global vasoconstriction and increases in systolic BP and HR, while spinal anesthesia and oxytocin caused arterial vasodilation and cardiac affection.
followup_time: Up to 5 minutes after the last intervention (oxytocin bolus)
